summary.tldr: Lets some people ask to serve a prison sentence in a designated addiction treatment facility, and changes correctional rules for those facilities.
what_it_does: Allows a sentencing court, on request, to recommend serving all or part of a sentence in a designated facility for addiction treatment, if the person has a pattern of substance use linked to the offence, agrees to treatment, and the offence meets set limits.
Requires courts that make a recommendation to send their reasons, related reports, and other relevant information to the Correctional Service of Canada.
Requires the Correctional Service of Canada to place the person in a designated facility as soon as reasonably possible after a recommendation.
Lets the Commissioner designate a penitentiary, or part of one, as an addiction treatment facility, and lets the minister make agreements with provinces to provide addiction treatment programs there.
Requires correctional plans and placement decisions to consider substance use, treatment programs, willingness to participate, and mental health assessments within 30 days of arrival.
Adds addiction treatment care in a designated facility to the Act’s definition of health care, and adds rules for moving inmates within a penitentiary to a designated facility.
